record.original_question: How reliable is analytic continuation from imaginary chemical potential once one moves beyond the small-µ/T regime where different fitting ansätze agree? In particular, can one control the strong fit-function dependence that appears when continuing pseudo-critical lines or other observables into the real-chemical-potential region?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum field theory (lattice QCD with $N_f$ flavors of quarks) whose grand-canonical partition function $Z(\mu)$ depends on a quark chemical potential $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$ at temperature $T>0$. For real $\mu$ the fermion determinant is complex (the sign problem), so direct Monte Carlo simulation is intractable; however, for purely imaginary chemical potential $\mu = i\mu_I$ with $\mu_I \in \mathbb{R}$ the measure is positive and observables $O(\mu_I/T)$ can be computed numerically. By the Roberge–Weiss symmetry, only the interval $\mu_I/T \in [0,\pi/3]$ carries independent information.

Let $O(x)$, $x = \mu/T$, denote an observable that is analytic in a neighborhood of $x=0$ (for instance the pseudo-critical temperature $T_c(\mu)/T_c(0)$ defining the chiral crossover line, or a susceptibility). Given a finite set of noisy numerical values $\{O(ix_k) \pm \sigma_k\}$ on a grid $x_k \in [0,\pi/3]$, one estimates $O$ for real $x$ by fitting an ansatz from a class $\mathcal{F}$ (e.g.\ polynomials in $x^2$, ratios of polynomials, trigonometric polynomials in $\mu_I/T$) and then evaluating the analytic continuation $x \mapsto x$ real.

Empirically, different ansätze in $\mathcal{F}$ yield mutually consistent extrapolations for $x \lesssim 0.3$ but diverge strongly for larger $x$, while the rigorous radius of convergence argument only guarantees control for $|x| < \pi/3$.

Problem. Develop a mathematically controlled procedure for analytic continuation of such observables from the imaginary-$\mu$ axis to the real-$\mu$ axis that:
(a) quantifies the systematic uncertainty arising from the choice of fitting ansatz in $\mathcal{F}$;
(b) provides rigorous error bars valid for $x \gtrsim 0.3$ and ideally up to $x \sim 1$;
(c) is consistent with the analyticity domain and known symmetries (Roberge–Weiss periodicity, charge-conjugation symmetry $O(\mu)=O(-\mu)$).

In particular, determine whether the strong fit-function dependence observed beyond $\mu/T \approx 0.3$ can be tamed, or prove a lower bound showing that with data restricted to $\mu_I/T \in [0,\pi/3]$ and finite precision $\sigma$, the extrapolation error necessarily grows uncontrollably for $\mu/T \gtrsim c$ for some explicit constant $c$.
artifact.status_search_result: The reliability of analytic continuation from imaginary chemical potential in finite-density lattice QCD remains an active and unresolved methodological issue. Recent lattice QCD reviews and studies (2022–2025) continue to report ansatz-dependent results for the curvature and higher-order coefficients of the pseudo-critical line beyond $\mu_B/T \gtrsim 2$–$3$ (i.e.\ $\mu_q/T \gtrsim 0.7$–$1$), and no rigorous procedure with controlled systematic error has been established. The problem is generally regarded as open.
